selected_hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy seasonal sakura-themed snacks and drinks, and soak in the festive atmosphere with locals and families. The park is free to enter and offers one of Japan's most iconic spring spectacles.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon), explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and street food stalls, and let kids try on samurai and kimono costumes at nearby rental shops. A perfect blend of history and family fun.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture with a self-guided or small-group tasting tour through Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and more. An incredible culinary adventure that introduces the whole family to authentic Japanese flavors and market culture.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo district, Tokyo

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A deeply moving and historically significant experience for families with older children. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and explore the museum which tells the story of August 6, 1945 with powerful exhibits promoting peace and reconciliation. An essential lesson in history and humanity that resonates long after the visit.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Stroll through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed natural wonders, especially stunning when cherry blossoms bloom nearby along the Oi River. Afterward, hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where kids can hand-feed wild Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below. A perfect mix of nature, culture, and family adventure.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel to accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Kansai International Airport at 13:00. Take the Haruka Express train to Kyoto Station (approx. 75 min, ~¥1,800 with IC card). Check in to Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Drop off luggage and freshen up. Take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park to see late cherry blossoms — the park is steps from your hotel and is one of Kyoto's most famous hanami (flower viewing) spots. The iconic weeping cherry tree is a must-see.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the atmospheric stone-paved lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka (Ninen-zaka & Sannen-zaka), a preserved historic street just 10 minutes from the hotel. Browse small craft shops and enjoy the lantern-lit ambiance. Head back toward Gion's Hanamikoji Street for a free evening stroll hoping to spot a geiko or maiko.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a convenience store onigiri and green tea at the airport (¥300–¥500).
meals.lunch: Grab a bento box or ramen at Kyoto Station's underground food hall (Porta or The Cube) before heading to hotel (¥800–¥1,200).
meals.dinner: Omen Noodles on Ninenzaka — a beloved local udon restaurant with hearty bowls from ¥1,100. Alternatively, pick up yakitori skewers and snacks from a Gion convenience store or Nishiki Market area stalls (¥600–¥1,000).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Suica or ICOCA IC card at Kansai Airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. April 15 may still have lingering cherry blossoms — check local bloom forecasts. Evening in Gion is free to walk and enjoy.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Fushimi Inari Taisha (free entry) — one of Japan's most iconic Shinto shrines with thousands of vermillion torii gates. Go early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat crowds. Hike as far up the mountain trail as energy allows — even 30–45 minutes up offers stunning views. Take the JR Nara Line from Tofukuji Station (5-min walk from hotel area) to Inari Station (2 stops, ¥150).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Kyoto and explore Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') — a narrow 400-meter covered market with over 100 stalls selling pickles, tofu, street food, and local snacks. Perfect for a cheap and delicious lunch crawl. Afterward, visit Kyoto's downtown Teramachi and Shinkyogoku shopping arcades for budget souvenir hunting.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Kiyomizudera Temple (¥500 entry) for the illuminated evening viewing if the special night lighting event is running in April. The hillside temple offers breathtaking views over Kyoto city lights. Walk back through Ninenzaka to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (7-Eleven or FamilyMart near hotel) — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and coffee (¥400–¥600).
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market food crawl — try tamagoyaki on a stick, pickled vegetables, and fresh tofu for ¥800–¥1,200 total.
meals.dinner: Ramen at Kyoto Ramen Koji (7th floor of Kyoto Station) or a local soba restaurant near Gion — budget ¥900–¥1,300.

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and open 24 hours. Kiyomizudera evening illumination events are seasonal — check the temple website closer to travel date. Wear comfortable walking shoes as this is a high-step day.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Arashiyama district via bus (City Bus #28 from Gion, ~40 min, ¥230). Visit the famous Arashiyama Bamboo Grove (free) first thing in the morning before crowds arrive. Walk through the towering green bamboo tunnels and continue to Tenryuji Temple Garden (¥500 garden entry — one of Kyoto's finest Zen gardens with a pond reflecting the Arashiyama mountains).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Arashiyama village streets. Visit Jojakko-ji Temple (¥500) — a quieter hillside temple with mossy stone steps and pagoda views, especially beautiful with spring foliage. Walk along the Oi River (Hozu River) banks and cross Togetsu-kyo Bridge — a classic postcard view. Browse the small artisan shops along Saga-Toriimoto Preserved Street.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion by bus. Enjoy the Gion Shirakawa canal area at dusk — willow trees, traditional machiya townhouses, and gentle stream lighting make this one of Kyoto's most romantic and photogenic spots. Free to walk and explore.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh-baked melon pan or a morning set at a local bakery near the hotel (¥400–¥600).
meals.lunch: Arashiyama tofu cuisine — Sagano-style yudofu (tofu hot pot) is a local specialty. Try a set lunch at a riverside restaurant for ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner in Gion — look for standing izakayas (tachinomi) or set-menu izakayas offering draft beer and small plates. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800 for food and one drink.

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is busy on weekends — arriving at the Bamboo Grove before 8:30 AM makes a significant difference. The City Bus One-Day Pass (¥700) is worthwhile if you plan multiple bus rides today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Imperial Palace Park (Kyoto Gyoen) — a vast free public park surrounding the former Imperial Palace. The park is spectacular in spring with cherry trees, plum blossoms, and open green lawns — ideal for families. Book a free guided tour of the Imperial Palace interior via the Imperial Household Agency website (advance reservation recommended). Take Bus #17 from Gion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or bus to the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) — a 2-km stone path along a canal lined with hundreds of cherry trees (late bloomers may still be visible in mid-April). The path connects Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion, ¥500 entry) to Nanzenji Temple (free grounds, ¥600 for main hall). Explore Nanzenji's impressive Sanmon gate and the surprising brick aqueduct running through the temple grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Maruyama Park for an evening hanami (flower viewing) picnic if blossoms remain. Pick up bento boxes, onigiri, and drinks from a nearby convenience store or supermarket and enjoy the park's festive lantern-lit atmosphere — a beloved local tradition.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) morning set — toast, egg, salad, and coffee for ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a cafe along the Philosopher's Path — many small cafes offer pasta, sandwiches, or Japanese sets for ¥900–¥1,300.
meals.dinner: Convenience store or supermarket picnic in Maruyama Park (¥600–¥1,000) — a quintessentially Japanese hanami experience.

day_by_day.notes: Kyoto Imperial Palace tours are free but require advance online reservation. Sunday can be crowded at popular sites — start early. Maruyama Park evening hanami is a wonderful family-friendly cultural experience unique to Japan's spring season.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara (45 min from Kyoto by Kintetsu Express, ~¥680 one way). Visit Nara Park first — hundreds of free-roaming sacred deer wander the park and will bow to receive deer crackers (shika senbei, ¥200/pack). This is a huge hit with families and children. Walk to Todai-ji Temple (¥600 entry), home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue — an awe-inspiring sight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine (free outer grounds, ¥500 for inner garden) — one of Japan's most important Shinto shrines, with hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns lining the approach path through ancient forest. Walk Naramachi, Nara's historic merchant district, with well-preserved machiya townhouses, small museums, and craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax with a walk through the quiet back streets of Gion, stopping at a local sento (public bath) for a traditional Japanese bathing experience (¥500–¥800). Ask hotel staff to recommend the nearest neighborhood sento.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel area convenience store before departure (¥400–¥600).
meals.lunch: Nara specialties — kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) from a local shop or a cheap set lunch near Todai-ji (¥900–¥1,400).
meals.dinner: Back in Kyoto — try obanzai (Kyoto-style home cooking) at a small local restaurant near Gion offering daily set meals (¥1,000–¥1,500).

day_by_day.notes: Nara deer are friendly but can be pushy around food — keep snacks secured, especially with young children. The Kintetsu Nara line from Kyoto is cheaper and more convenient than JR for this trip. Buy return tickets at the station.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the northern Higashiyama district on foot from the hotel. Visit Chion-in Temple (free grounds, ¥500 for inner garden) — one of Japan's most impressive temple complexes with a massive sanmon gate (the largest wooden gate in Japan). Continue to Shoren-in Temple (¥500) — famous for its enormous 800-year-old camphor trees at the entrance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Heian Jingu Shrine (free entry to outer grounds, ¥600 for garden) — a grand vermillion shrine built in 1895 to commemorate Kyoto's 1,100th anniversary. The surrounding Okazaki area has several free or low-cost museums. Visit the Kyoto Municipal Museum of Art or the National Museum of Modern Art (¥430) if interested in Japanese art and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining alley parallel to the Kamo River, packed with restaurants ranging from budget ramen to upscale kaiseki. Watch the sunset from Kamo River's Sanjo or Shijo bridge — locals sit along the riverbanks in the evening, a beloved Kyoto tradition.

meals.breakfast: Japanese-style breakfast at a local kissaten — miso soup, rice, grilled fish set (¥600–¥900).
meals.lunch: Cheap teishoku (set meal) at a neighborhood shokudo (diner) near Okazaki — rice, miso, main dish for ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Budget-friendly ramen or gyoza restaurant in Pontocho or along the Kamo River — ¥900–¥1,300.

day_by_day.notes: Pontocho is best experienced at dusk when lanterns light up the narrow alley. Sitting by the Kamo River at sunset is a free and quintessentially Kyoto experience beloved by locals and visitors alike.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Osaka (15 min from Kyoto by Shinkansen or 30 min by Hankyu/JR, ¥560–¥1,420). Head to Osaka Castle (¥600 museum entry, park free) — a magnificent reconstructed castle surrounded by a moat and beautiful park. April may still offer cherry blossoms in the castle park. The museum inside offers excellent English displays on the castle's history and the Sengoku period.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dotonbori — Osaka's iconic entertainment and food district. Walk along the canal beneath the giant Glico running man sign. Browse Shinsaibashi shopping arcade. Visit Kuromon Ichiba Market ('Osaka's Kitchen') for street food sampling — try takoyaki (octopus balls), kushikatsu (fried skewers), and fresh seafood.
day_by_day.evening: Climb Tsutenkaku Tower (¥900) in the retro Shinsekai neighborhood for panoramic city views, then explore the quirky, nostalgic streets below full of cheap kushikatsu restaurants and old-school arcades. Return to Kyoto by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Grab food before departure at Kyoto Station convenience store (¥400–¥600).
meals.lunch: Dotonbori street food lunch — takoyaki (¥600), okonomiyaki (¥800), and fresh tamagoyaki. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a satisfying food crawl.
meals.dinner: Kushikatsu dinner in Shinsekai — a full meal of fried skewers with unlimited cabbage and dipping sauce for ¥1,200–¥1,800.

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is extremely family-friendly and the food scene is one of Japan's best for budget travelers. The phrase 'kuidaore' (eat until you drop) is Osaka's motto. Keep the Dotonbori double-dipping rule in mind at kushikatsu restaurants — never dip a skewer twice into the shared sauce!

day_by_day.morning: Visit Daitokuji Temple Complex (free grounds) in northern Kyoto — a vast Zen Buddhist complex with 22 sub-temples, several open to the public for ¥400–¥600 each. Zuiho-in and Koto-in are particularly beautiful with moss gardens and raked gravel. Take Bus #12 from Gion. This is one of Kyoto's most serene and crowd-free cultural experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kinkakuji (Golden Pavilion, ¥500) — Kyoto's most iconic sight, a gold-leaf-covered Zen temple reflecting in a still pond. Then walk or take a short bus ride to Ryoanji Temple (¥600) — home to Japan's most famous rock garden, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Contemplate the 15 stones arranged in raked white gravel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion. Visit a local supermarket (look for Fresco or Gyomu Super) in the early evening when bento boxes and prepared foods are discounted 20–50% — a great budget dinner strategy. Enjoy dinner in the hotel room or in Maruyama Park.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri and miso soup from convenience store (¥350–¥500).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a Kyoto supermarket or convenience store eaten in Daitokuji's peaceful garden grounds (¥500–¥800).
meals.dinner: Discounted supermarket bento and side dishes (¥600–¥1,000) — look for the yellow discount stickers after 17:00–18:00.

day_by_day.notes: Daitokuji is far less visited than Kinkakuji and offers a more authentic Zen atmosphere. The combination of Kinkakuji and Ryoanji is a classic Kyoto afternoon. Northern Kyoto requires bus travel — consider a day bus pass (¥700) if making multiple trips.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Ward's Gekkeikan Okura Sake Museum (¥600, includes sake tasting) — learn about Kyoto's 400-year sake brewing tradition in the historic Fushimi sake district. Walk along the scenic Horikawa Canal lined with willow trees and old sake warehouse walls. Take the Kintetsu line to Momoyama-Mihara or Kintetsu-Tanbabashi Station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Kyoto and visit Tofukuji Temple (¥600) — a massive Zen temple complex famous for its wooden Sanmon gate (National Treasure), beautiful Zen gardens, and the impressive Tsutenkyo Bridge walkway connecting the main hall to the sub-temples. Tofukuji is very close to the hotel/Gion area.
day_by_day.evening: Final proper evening in Gion — walk Hanamikoji Street one last time as the teahouses light up for the evening. Visit a local craft shop to pick up last-minute omiyage (souvenirs) — Kyoto specialties include yatsuhashi sweets, Nishijin textiles, and kyo-sensu folding fans. Enjoy a relaxed farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Sit-down breakfast at a local kissaten for a proper morning send-off (¥600–¥900).
meals.lunch: Fushimi area soba or udon lunch near the sake district (¥800–¥1,200).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range izakaya in Gion — splurge slightly for the last night with yakitori, edamame, cold tofu, and sake or Kirin beer (¥1,500–¥2,500).

day_by_day.notes: The Gekkeikan Sake Museum is a hidden gem that most tourists skip — the ¥600 entry includes a small bottle of sake or amazake (sweet non-alcoholic sake), making it great value. Tofukuji is one of Kyoto's most underrated temples. Buy omiyage at Nishiki Market or station shops for the best selection and prices.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last peaceful walk through Maruyama Park and the surrounding Higashiyama temples before checkout. Visit Yasaka Shrine (free, open 24 hours) adjacent to Maruyama Park — a beautiful and historically significant shrine that marks the heart of Gion. Light an incense stick and say goodbye to Kyoto.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of hotel. Store luggage at Kyoto Station coin lockers (¥400–¥700/day). Spend remaining time browsing Kyoto Station's expansive shopping complex — The Cube and Porta underground malls have excellent food and souvenir selections. Pick up last-minute gifts: matcha Kit Kats, Kyoto-brand sweets, and local teas make affordable and popular souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for airport based on onward flight schedule. Take the Haruka Express from Kyoto Station to Kansai International Airport (75 min, ~¥1,800). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Final convenience store breakfast or hotel area cafe — savor one last onigiri and canned coffee (¥400–¥600).
meals.lunch: Kyoto Station food hall lunch — try a Kyoto-style kaiseki bento box from one of the station's many vendors as a final treat (¥1,000–¥1,500).
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Kansai International — ramen or udon at a terminal restaurant (¥900–¥1,400), or pick up an airport bento for the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Coin lockers at Kyoto Station fill up quickly on weekends — arrive early or use the larger lockers on the Shinkansen concourse level. The Haruka Express to KIX requires a reserved seat — book at the green ticket machines or JR ticket counter. Confirm flight departure time and allow ample buffer for international check-in procedures.

trip_options.title: Classic Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Stroll through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed natural wonders, especially stunning when cherry blossoms bloom nearby along the Oi River. Afterward, hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where kids can hand-feed wild Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below. A perfect mix of nature, culture, and family adventure.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight lands at 13:00, so morning is in-transit. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Haruka Express or airport limousine bus toward Kyoto. Journey takes approximately 75 minutes from Kansai Airport or 2.5 hours from Narita.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district (check-in typically from 15:00). Once settled, take a gentle introductory stroll through Maruyama Park to see the iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) — mid-April is peak or late bloom season. Absorb the relaxed hanami atmosphere, watch locals picnicking under the blossoms, and get your bearings in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the stone-paved lanes of Gion's Hanamikoji Street at dusk — the lantern-lit teahouses and preserved machiya townhouses are enchanting. Keep an eye out for geiko or maiko heading to evening engagements. Enjoy a quiet first dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab an onigiri and green tea from a convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) at the airport — a classic Japanese travel ritual.
meals.lunch: Pick up a bento box at the train station (ekiben) during your journey to Kyoto — stations like Shin-Osaka have excellent options for ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Omen Noodles on Ninenzaka — a beloved local udon restaurant near Gion. Warm, hearty, and budget-friendly at around ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person. No reservations needed.

day_by_day.notes: Buy an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at the airport for seamless transit payments throughout the trip. April 15 is typically within Kyoto's cherry blossom window — check Japan Meteorological Corporation bloom forecasts upon arrival. Keep Day 1 light; jet lag will be a factor.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Featured Experience) — Start early (8:00 AM) before crowds build. Spread a picnic blanket under the famous weeping cherry tree, sip canned coffee or tea from a nearby vending machine, and experience hanami the authentic way. The morning light through the blossoms is spectacular for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Higashiyama Cultural District on foot — walk from Maruyama Park south through Chion-in Temple (one of Japan's grandest temple gates), along Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka cobblestone paths, past Kiyomizudera Temple's famous wooden stage overlooking the city. Allow 3–4 hours for this scenic cultural walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion for the evening. Visit Yasaka Shrine, which borders Maruyama Park and is beautifully illuminated at night during cherry blossom season. Explore the atmospheric Pontocho alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining corridor running parallel to the Kamo River — for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel if included, or visit a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near Gion for toast, egg, and coffee (morning set, ¥600–¥900).
meals.lunch: Yudofu (tofu hot pot) at Junsei near Nanzenji — a Kyoto specialty perfectly suited to the cultural district walk. Set lunches run ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Pontocho dining — choose a mid-range restaurant along the alley with riverside seating (kawadoko). Grilled skewers (yakitori) or kaiseki-lite set menus available for ¥2,000–¥4,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Higashiyama involves significant uphill cobblestone paths. Kiyomizudera charges a ¥500 admission fee. Morning visits to Maruyama Park are free. The park is illuminated at night during hanami season — worth a brief after-dinner return visit.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park (Featured Experience) — Take the city bus or Randen tram to Arashiyama (30–40 minutes from Gion). Arrive by 8:00–8:30 AM to beat the crowds at the bamboo grove. The towering green stalks create an otherworldly corridor. Afterward, climb to Iwatayama Monkey Park (¥550 adults, ¥250 children) for panoramic views of Kyoto and close encounters with Japanese macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Arashiyama further — visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its UNESCO-listed garden (¥500), stroll along the Oi River, and browse artisan shops along Saga-Toriimoto preserved street. Optionally rent a rowboat on the river for a family-friendly activity (¥1,500–¥2,000 for 30 minutes).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion/central Kyoto. Visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's 'Kitchen' — a narrow five-block covered market with over 100 stalls selling pickles, sweets, tofu, and street food. Perfect for grazing and souvenir shopping before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store or hotel breakfast before departing for Arashiyama.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant in Arashiyama — try Yoshida-ya for tofu cuisine or grab yudofu and warabi mochi (bracken-starch sweets) from market stalls along the main street. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner near Gion — Torisei is a renowned local yakitori and sake bar. Expect ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Arashiyama will be busy — an early start is essential. The Monkey Park involves a 20-minute uphill hike; bring water. Nishiki Market closes most stalls by 18:00, so plan accordingly. Arashiyama cherry blossoms along the riverbank are stunning in mid-April.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — Take the JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station to Inari Station (5 minutes, ¥150). Hike through the iconic thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up Mount Inari. The full hike takes 2–3 hours; families can turn back at Yotsutsuji intersection (45 minutes up) for great views without the full climb. Free entry, open 24 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Nara (45 minutes from Kyoto by Kintetsu or JR line). Visit Nara Park — home to over 1,000 free-roaming sika deer considered sacred messengers. Children absolutely love feeding them deer crackers (shika senbei, ¥200). Walk to Todai-ji Temple, housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue (¥600 admission). Explore the peaceful Kasuga Taisha Shrine lantern-lined paths.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax with a stroll along the Kamo River — locals gather on the riverbanks at dusk in a beloved Kyoto tradition. Enjoy a quieter Sunday evening dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or a nearby bakery — Kyoto has excellent French-Japanese fusion bakeries (Pain de Sucre near Gion is a local favorite, ¥400–¥700).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nara — Maguro Koya offers excellent value teishoku (set meals) near Nara Park, or try kakinoha-zushi (persimmon-leaf sushi), a Nara specialty, from a market stall. ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Ramen dinner back in Kyoto — Kyoto-style ramen features a rich chicken or pork broth with thin noodles. Ippudo or a local shop near Shijo-Kawaramachi. ¥900–¥1,300.

day_by_day.notes: Deer in Nara bow for crackers but can be pushy — supervise young children. Todai-ji has a narrow wooden pillar with a hole said to bring good luck to those who crawl through it (sized for children). Book nothing in advance for today — all sites are walk-in. Fushimi Inari is best early morning or late afternoon to avoid tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Kyoto Imperial Palace and Kyoto Gyoen National Garden — The surrounding Imperial Garden (free) is a vast green space with cherry and plum trees, perfect for a morning walk. The Imperial Palace itself requires advance reservation (free via Imperial Household Agency website) or join a walk-in tour at 10:00 or 14:00. A dignified, historically rich experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nijo Castle (Nijojo) — A 15-minute bus ride from the Imperial Palace. This UNESCO World Heritage Site was the Kyoto residence of the Tokugawa shoguns. Famous for its 'nightingale floors' designed to squeak as an intruder alarm, stunning painted fusuma screens, and beautiful garden. Admission ¥1,030 adults, ¥350 children.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Kawaramachi/Shijo shopping and entertainment district for the evening. Browse department stores (Takashimaya, Daimaru), walk the covered Teramachi and Shinkyogoku shopping arcades, and enjoy the lively Monday evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Japanese morning set at a nearby kissaten — miso soup, rice, grilled fish, and pickles (¥700–¥1,000).
meals.lunch: Obanzai cuisine — Kyoto's traditional home-style cooking featuring small seasonal vegetable and tofu dishes. Eat at a lunch counter near Nijo Castle. ¥1,200–¥2,000 for a set.
meals.dinner: Conveyor-belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) at Musashi Sushi near Kawaramachi — a fun, family-friendly, and budget-conscious option. Plates from ¥130–¥500 each; expect to spend ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Nijo Castle's nightingale floors are a genuine highlight for children and adults alike — listen carefully as you walk. The Imperial Palace tour is conducted in Japanese with English pamphlets available; an audio guide app is recommended. Monday is a good day for popular sites as some tourists depart on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Travel Day: Kyoto → Hiroshima via Shinkansen (Nozomi/Sakura, approximately 45 minutes, ¥5,720–¥11,000 with JR Pass). Check out of your Kyoto boutique stay and store luggage at Hiroshima Station coin lockers upon arrival. Begin the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park experience (Featured Experience).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park (Featured Experience) — Walk through the haunting and deeply moving Peace Memorial Park. Visit the A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), the only structure left standing near the hypocenter, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Enter the Peace Memorial Museum (¥200 admission) — exhibits include personal artifacts, testimonies, and the story of the atomic bombing. A profoundly important historical experience for families with children aged 10+.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry (15 minutes, ¥180) from Hiroshima to Miyajima Island. Check in to a Miyajima ryokan or guesthouse for a 1-night stay (mid-range option: Miyajima Morinoyado or similar, ¥12,000–¥18,000 per room). Stroll to the famous floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine, beautifully illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Kyoto Station before your Shinkansen — excellent ekiben options or a sit-down café in the station.
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki near the Peace Park — the local version layers noodles, cabbage, egg, and toppings on a griddle. Completely different from Osaka style and a must-try. ¥900–¥1,400 at Okonomimura (a multi-floor okonomiyaki village).
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Miyajima ryokan (often included in room rate) or at a local restaurant featuring Hiroshima oysters — Miyajima is famous for them. Grilled, fried, or in hot pot. ¥1,500–¥3,000.

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is emotionally intense — prepare children in advance and allow time for quiet reflection afterward. The museum is well-curated and not gratuitously graphic, but deeply impactful. Miyajima's torii gate is best seen at high tide when it appears to float — check tide tables in advance. Deer also roam freely on Miyajima Island.

day_by_day.morning: Miyajima Island Exploration — Visit Itsukushima Shrine (¥300 admission) in the morning light before tour groups arrive. Hike or take the ropeway (¥1,800 round trip) up Mount Misen for panoramic views of the Seto Inland Sea and surrounding islands. The summit offers a sacred eternal flame said to have burned for 1,200 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hiroshima by ferry, then take the Shinkansen to Osaka (approximately 1 hour 20 minutes, ¥5,720). Check in to your Osaka accommodation (mid-range hotel in Namba or Shinsaibashi area recommended). Explore Dotonbori — Osaka's neon-lit entertainment and food district along the canal.
day_by_day.evening: Full Dotonbori immersion — see the famous Glico Running Man sign, Kani Doraku crab, and Ebisu Bridge. This is Osaka's beating heart. Try multiple street foods as you wander: takoyaki (octopus balls), kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers), and taiyaki (fish-shaped sweets).

meals.breakfast: Ryokan breakfast if included — a traditional Japanese spread of grilled fish, rice, miso, and pickles. Otherwise, grab food at Miyajima ferry terminal shops.
meals.lunch: Momiji manju (maple-leaf-shaped cakes filled with red bean paste) — Miyajima's iconic souvenir snack — plus oyster street food before departing the island. ¥200–¥800.
meals.dinner: Dotonbori street food feast — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person grazing through takoyaki (¥500–¥700 for 6 pieces), kushikatsu at a standing bar, and fresh crab if budget allows.

day_by_day.notes: Miyajima has no cars — it's a wonderfully peaceful walking island. The ropeway closes in bad weather. Osaka's Dotonbori is best experienced in the evening when all the neon signs are blazing. Osaka has a reputation as Japan's food capital — pace yourself for two days of exceptional eating.

day_by_day.morning: Osaka Castle (Osaka-jo) — A 20-minute subway ride from Namba. The reconstructed castle is one of Japan's most iconic, surrounded by a moat and cherry blossom trees (late bloom may still be visible in mid-April). The interior museum (¥600) traces the history of Toyotomi Hideyoshi and the castle's role in unifying Japan. The top-floor observation deck offers city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shinsekai District and Tsutenkaku Tower — Take the subway to this retro 1950s-themed neighborhood. Climb Tsutenkaku Tower (¥900) for views and interact with the Billiken luck statue. Eat kushikatsu (a Shinsekai specialty — never double-dip the sauce!) at a local standing restaurant. Browse the wonderfully kitschy shops.
day_by_day.evening: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan (optional for families with young children, ¥2,400 adults / ¥1,200 children) in the Tempozan Harbor area, or return to Namba for shopping at Don Quijote (the everything store, open until 5 AM) and evening entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a convenience store morning routine — Japan's convenience store onigiri, sandwiches, and hot foods are genuinely excellent and cost ¥400–¥700.
meals.lunch: Kushikatsu lunch in Shinsekai — a set of 10–15 skewers with sides costs ¥1,200–¥2,000. Daruma is the most famous chain; Yaekatsu is a beloved local alternative.
meals.dinner: Kuromon Ichiba Market dinner — Osaka's 'Kitchen' market (closes around 18:00 for stalls, some restaurants open later). Fresh sashimi, grilled scallops, and wagyu beef skewers eaten standing at market counters. ¥2,000–¥3,500.

day_by_day.notes: Osaka Castle grounds are free to enter; the tower museum has a fee. The castle park may still have late-blooming cherry trees in mid-April — a lovely bonus. Shinsekai has a rough-and-ready charm that contrasts beautifully with polished Kyoto. Keep valuables secure in busy Dotonbori at night, though Osaka is very safe overall.

day_by_day.morning: Travel Day: Osaka → Tokyo via Shinkansen Nozomi (2 hours 30 minutes, ¥14,720 or covered by JR Pass). Arrive at Tokyo Station by mid-morning. Check in to Tokyo accommodation (mid-range hotel in Asakusa or Shinjuku recommended). Head immediately to Asakusa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street (Featured Experience) — Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Pass through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) with its massive red lantern. Walk the 250-meter Nakamise shopping street lined with stalls selling traditional crafts, ningyo-yaki cakes, and souvenirs. Explore the temple grounds, draw an omikuji fortune slip (¥100), and soak in the atmosphere of old Tokyo (Shitamachi).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Asakusa further — visit Nakamise after the daytime crowds thin, walk along the Sumida River, and see Senso-ji beautifully illuminated at night. Optionally take a short taxi or subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) for an evening of electronics, anime, and gaming culture — a unique Tokyo experience.

meals.breakfast: Shinkansen ekiben from Osaka Station — a final taste of Kansai cuisine to enjoy on the bullet train.
meals.lunch: Asakusa lunch — Daikokuya Tempura (established 1887) serves legendary tempura donburi (tendon) for ¥1,500–¥2,500. Expect a short queue; worth it.
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner in Asakusa's backstreets — the area around Hoppy Street has lively, affordable izakayas with outdoor seating, cold beer, and grilled skewers. ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Store large luggage at Tokyo Station coin lockers (¥400–¥700/day) while you explore Asakusa if check-in isn't available yet. Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours (main hall has specific hours). The Nakamise shops close around 17:00–18:00. Asakusa rickshaw rides are available for a fun family experience (¥3,000–¥8,000 depending on route).

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (Featured Experience) — Start early at 8:00 AM at Tokyo's legendary food market (the inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains). Self-guided tasting tour through stalls and shops: fresh tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), sushi, grilled scallops, matcha sweets, and premium dashi. A feast for all senses and a perfect final Tokyo morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shibuya and Harajuku — Take the subway to Shibuya. Cross the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing (best viewed from Starbucks or Mag's Park above). Walk up to Harajuku's Takeshita Street for youth fashion and crepes, then stroll the elegant Omotesando boulevard for window shopping and people-watching. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine — a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji, a peaceful counterpoint to the urban energy around it.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — return to your hotel to freshen up, then head to Shinjuku for a farewell dinner. Visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, open until 22:30 on most nights) for a stunning nighttime panorama of the city. End the trip with a memorable dinner in Shinjuku's Golden Gai or Kabukicho area.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market grazing IS breakfast — fresh uni (sea urchin), tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki, and green tea. Budget ¥1,500–¥3,000 for a thorough tasting tour.
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepes (a Tokyo institution, ¥500–¥900) plus ramen in Shibuya or Harajuku — Ichiran Ramen offers individual booths for a uniquely Japanese solo-focus dining experience. ¥900–¥1,300.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Tokyo restaurant — try sukiyaki or shabu-shabu (Japanese hot pot) at a restaurant in Shinjuku. Shabusen or Nabezo offer all-you-can-eat options for ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person — a festive and interactive final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest 8:00–10:00 AM — arrive early for the best selection and shortest queues. Meiji Jingu is free to enter and offers a peaceful forest walk (the surrounding Yoyogi Park may have late cherry blossoms). Pack any purchased food items carefully for the flight home — many Tsukiji vendors sell vacuum-sealed products suitable for travel. Check flight departure time and plan airport transfer accordingly (allow 90 minutes from central Tokyo to Narita, 60 minutes to Haneda).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy seasonal sakura-themed snacks and drinks, and soak in the festive atmosphere with locals and families. The park is free to enter and offers one of Japan's most iconic spring spectacles.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon), explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and street food stalls, and let kids try on samurai and kimono costumes at nearby rental shops. A perfect blend of history and family fun.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture with a self-guided or small-group tasting tour through Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and more. An incredible culinary adventure that introduces the whole family to authentic Japanese flavors and market culture.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo district, Tokyo

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A deeply moving and historically significant experience for families with older children. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and explore the museum which tells the story of August 6, 1945 with powerful exhibits promoting peace and reconciliation. An essential lesson in history and humanity that resonates long after the visit.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Stroll through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed natural wonders, especially stunning when cherry blossoms bloom nearby along the Oi River. Afterward, hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where kids can hand-feed wild Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below. A perfect mix of nature, culture, and family adventure.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer from the airport to your boutique stay in the Gion district, Kyoto. Settle into your room and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle Introduction to Gion — After check-in, take a leisurely stroll through the iconic Gion district. Explore the historic Hanamikoji Street lined with traditional ochaya (teahouses), admire the preserved machiya townhouses, and soak in the atmosphere of Japan's most famous geisha quarter. If lucky, spot a maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to an evening engagement.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Just steps from your hotel, experience the magical hanami tradition beneath Kyoto's most celebrated weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura), beautifully illuminated after dark. The night-time lighting (yozakura) transforms the park into an ethereal wonderland.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light meal on board or at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Izuju (いづ重) — A Kyoto institution near Gion serving exquisite pressed sushi (oshizushi) in an elegant traditional setting.
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Honten — A three-Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in Higashiyama, just minutes from your hotel. Reserve well in advance for a multi-course seasonal tasting menu featuring spring delicacies.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance through your hotel concierge. Confirm cherry blossom bloom status upon arrival — mid-April in Kyoto typically offers late-season blossoms. Pack a light layer for evening park viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha — Rise early (by 7:00 AM) to beat the crowds at Kyoto's most iconic shrine. Hike through the seemingly endless tunnel of vermillion torii gates winding up Mount Inari. The lower trails take about 30–45 minutes; the full summit hike is 2–3 hours. Early morning mist adds a mystical quality rarely captured in photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market & Teramachi Shopping Arcade — Return to central Kyoto and explore Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen'), a narrow five-block covered market offering premium Japanese pickles, fresh tofu, matcha sweets, and seasonal delicacies. Browse the adjacent Teramachi arcade for artisan crafts, ceramics, and lacquerware as premium souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Kiyomizu-dera Temple at Dusk — Visit the UNESCO World Heritage wooden stage temple perched on the hillside of Higashiyama. The approach through Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka stone-paved lanes is lined with traditional shops and teahouses. The temple is often illuminated during cherry blossom season for special evening viewing.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or Sarasa Nishijin — a beautifully converted sento (bathhouse) café serving artisan coffee and morning pastries.
meals.lunch: Tempura Yoshikawa — A beloved Kyoto tempura restaurant offering counter-style dining where the chef prepares each piece fresh before you.
meals.dinner: Mizai — A Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in Higashiyama offering an intimate, seasonal multi-course experience. Alternatively, dine at Gion Nanba for refined Kyoto cuisine in a century-old machiya.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for Fushimi Inari. The hike can be muddy after rain. Book dinner reservations at least 2–3 weeks in advance through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Tenryu-ji Garden — Head west to Arashiyama for an early morning walk through the iconic bamboo grove, best experienced before 9:00 AM when crowds are thin and light filters beautifully through the stalks. Follow with a visit to Tenryu-ji, a UNESCO World Heritage Zen temple with a stunning garden reflecting the Arashiyama mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arashiyama Monkey Park Iwatayama — A family-friendly highlight: hike a 20-minute trail up the mountain to encounter over 120 wild Japanese macaques roaming freely. Views over Kyoto from the summit are spectacular. Descend and explore the charming Arashiyama riverside, rent a traditional wooden boat, or browse artisan shops along Togetsukyo Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion for a Private Maiko Experience — Arrange through your hotel a private ozashiki (banquet) experience with a maiko or geiko in a traditional ochaya. Enjoy traditional dance performances, sake, and intimate conversation — a rare and deeply cultural luxury experience unavailable to the general public.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Arabica Kyoto Arashiyama — A world-renowned specialty coffee shop with riverside views, perfect before the bamboo grove.
meals.lunch: Shigetsu at Tenryu-ji — A refined shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) restaurant within the temple grounds, offering a serene and authentic cultural dining experience.
meals.dinner: Private ozashiki banquet dinner included in the maiko experience, featuring traditional Kyoto cuisine served by your maiko host. Supplement with a nightcap at Bar K6 in Gion, a sophisticated whisky bar.

day_by_day.notes: The private maiko experience must be booked weeks in advance through a licensed teahouse agency or your hotel concierge — this is not publicly bookable. Comfortable shoes essential for Monkey Park trail.

day_by_day.morning: Nijo Castle & Nishiki Market Revisit — Visit Nijo Castle, the opulent Edo-period residence of the Tokugawa shoguns. Explore the ornate Ninomaru Palace with its famous 'nightingale floors' that chirp underfoot (a security measure against intruders), and stroll the expansive castle gardens, which may still show late cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Philosopher's Path & Nanzen-ji Temple — Walk the famous Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-michi), a 2km stone path along a canal lined with cherry trees in various stages of bloom and petal fall. End at the grand Nanzen-ji Zen temple complex, exploring its impressive Sanmon gate, aqueduct ruins, and sub-temples including Tenjuan garden.
day_by_day.evening: Pontocho Alley Dining — Explore Pontocho, Kyoto's most atmospheric dining alley running parallel to the Kamo River. In warmer months, many restaurants extend 'kawadoko' riverside terraces over the water. Choose a premium restaurant for a memorable riverside evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel's in-room dining service or Cafe Bibliotic Hello! — a charming café in a converted machiya near the city center.
meals.lunch: Omen Nanzenji — A beloved noodle restaurant near Nanzen-ji serving hearty udon in a rustic, warm setting.
meals.dinner: Kichisen (吉泉) — One of Kyoto's most revered three-Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurants in Pontocho, offering the pinnacle of Japanese haute cuisine. Alternatively, Pontocho Kanani for elegant multi-course French-Japanese fusion with river views.

day_by_day.notes: Nijo Castle can be busy on weekends — arrive early. The Philosopher's Path is most magical in early morning light. Kawadoko terraces are weather-dependent; confirm availability with your chosen restaurant.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nara — Take a 45-minute express train to Nara, Japan's ancient capital. Visit Todai-ji Temple, home to the world's largest bronze Buddha statue (Daibutsu), and roam Nara Park where over 1,200 freely wandering sacred deer will approach you for special deer crackers (shika senbei). A wonderfully family-friendly experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kasuga Taisha & Naramachi — Explore the atmospheric Kasuga Grand Shrine, a UNESCO site draped in hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns. Wander through Naramachi, Nara's beautifully preserved merchant district, browsing traditional craft shops and artisan studios before returning to Kyoto by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxation Evening at Your Boutique Hotel — After a full day of travel, enjoy an in-hotel experience. Request an in-room kaiseki dinner service or visit the hotel's onsen (hot spring bath) if available. Alternatively, enjoy a quiet evening stroll through Maruyama Park to admire the illuminated cherry trees one more time.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before departing for Nara.
meals.lunch: Edosan Nara — A refined restaurant near Todai-ji serving traditional Nara cuisine including kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) and local specialties in a historic setting.
meals.dinner: In-room kaiseki dinner arranged through your hotel concierge, or Hyotei (表木) — a legendary three-Michelin-starred Kyoto restaurant serving breakfast kaiseki, also available for dinner by special arrangement.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase deer crackers only from official vendors in Nara Park. Deer can be assertive — keep bags closed and be mindful with young children. The Kintetsu Limited Express from Kyoto to Nara is the most comfortable option.

day_by_day.morning: Shinkansen to Tokyo — Check out from your Kyoto boutique stay and board the Nozomi Shinkansen (bullet train) from Kyoto Station to Tokyo Station (~2h 15min). Reserve Green Car (first class) seats for maximum comfort and enjoy Mt. Fuji views on the right side of the train on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa District — Arrive in Tokyo and check into your luxury Tokyo hotel (arrange in advance). Head immediately to Asakusa to visit Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple. Walk the iconic Nakamise Shopping Street for premium traditional crafts, ningyo-yaki sweets, and artisan goods. Explore the surrounding Asakusa district with its rickshaws, traditional craft shops, and old-Tokyo atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Skytree Observation Deck — A short walk from Asakusa, ascend the Tokyo Skytree (634m) for breathtaking panoramic views of the Tokyo skyline at golden hour and into the evening. Reserve the Tembo Galleria (450m) for the highest views. The contrast of ancient Asakusa below and the modern megalopolis stretching to the horizon is unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Kyoto hotel before checkout, or grab an ekiben (premium train bento) at Kyoto Station for the Shinkansen journey.
meals.lunch: Asakusa Imahan — A celebrated sukiyaki and shabu-shabu restaurant near Senso-ji, serving premium Wagyu beef in a traditional setting since 1895.
meals.dinner: Ryugin (龍吟) — A three-Michelin-starred innovative Japanese cuisine restaurant in Roppongi, offering a theatrical multi-course experience that reinterprets Japanese culinary tradition.

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen Green Car seats in advance, especially for a Tuesday. Pre-book Tokyo Skytree Tembo Galleria tickets online to avoid queues. Confirm Tokyo hotel check-in time and arrange luggage forwarding (takuhaibin) if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Begin the morning with a self-guided or private guide-led tasting tour through the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample premium tamagoyaki (Japanese omelette), fresh uni (sea urchin), wagyu skewers, and world-class sushi at the market's renowned breakfast counters. This is an immersive dive into Tokyo's extraordinary food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets — Experience one of Tokyo's most extraordinary digital art installations. TeamLab creates immersive, interactive environments where art responds to your movement — a magical, otherworldly experience beloved by families and adults alike. Book tickets well in advance as they frequently sell out.
day_by_day.evening: Ginza Luxury District & Kabuki-za Theatre — Stroll through Ginza, Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district, exploring flagship stores of Hermès, Chanel, and Japanese luxury brands. Attend a performance at the historic Kabuki-za Theatre (single-act tickets available for non-Japanese speakers) for an authentic encounter with Japan's most dramatic traditional performing art.

meals.breakfast: Premium sushi breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi (arrive early; queues form before opening). Alternatively, Tsukiji Tamazushi for a slightly shorter wait.
meals.lunch: Kyubey Ginza — A legendary high-end sushi restaurant in Ginza with over 80 years of history, serving omakase (chef's selection) courses of impeccable Edo-mae sushi.
meals.dinner: Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (if reservable through hotel concierge) or Sushi Yoshitake — a three-Michelin-starred Ginza sushi counter for an intimate, world-class omakase experience.

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab tickets must be booked online weeks in advance. Kabuki-za single-act (hitomaku) tickets are sold same-day at the fourth-floor box office — arrive 30 minutes before the act begins. English audio guides available.

day_by_day.morning: Meiji Jingu Shrine & Harajuku — Begin with a serene morning visit to Meiji Jingu, Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine, set within a vast forested park offering a peaceful escape from the city. Walk the grand gravel path through towering cedar trees. Afterward, explore the adjacent Harajuku area, including the charming Omotesando Hills luxury shopping complex and the tree-lined Omotesando boulevard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shibuya & Shinjuku Exploration — Experience the iconic Shibuya Crossing, the world's busiest pedestrian scramble, from the observation deck of Shibuya Sky for an aerial perspective. Continue to Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) for atmosphere, and explore the vast Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, which may still offer late cherry blossoms or beautiful spring greenery.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Helicopter Tour (Optional Premium Add-on) — For an extraordinary luxury experience, book a private evening helicopter tour over the Tokyo skyline, seeing the illuminated metropolis, Tokyo Tower, Rainbow Bridge, and Mt. Fuji silhouette from above. Alternatively, enjoy cocktails at the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar (featured in Lost in Translation) for iconic city views.

meals.breakfast: The Prince Gallery Tokyo Kioicho — Enjoy a refined breakfast at your luxury hotel or the hotel's signature restaurant with panoramic city views.
meals.lunch: Harajuku Gyoza Lou — A beloved local institution for perfectly crispy gyoza, or Anniversaire Café on Omotesando for an elegant French-Japanese brunch.
meals.dinner: Quintessence (クインテッセンス) — A three-Michelin-starred French restaurant in Shirokanedai offering a single, extraordinary tasting menu of French cuisine elevated with Japanese precision and seasonal ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter; the inner garden (Gyoen) charges a small fee. Shibuya Sky observation deck tickets should be reserved online. Helicopter tours require advance booking through specialist operators — your hotel concierge can arrange.

day_by_day.morning: Hiroshima Day Trip — Take the early Shinkansen from Tokyo to Hiroshima (~4 hours on Nozomi). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Peace Memorial Park — a profoundly moving and historically significant experience, particularly meaningful for families with older children. The A-Bomb Dome, Eternal Flame, and Children's Peace Monument offer powerful perspectives on history and humanity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Miyajima Island — Take a short ferry to Miyajima Island to see the iconic 'floating' torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The vermillion gate rising from the sea is one of Japan's most iconic images. Explore the shrine, encounter the island's friendly deer, and hike or cable-car up Mount Misen for panoramic views over the Seto Inland Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo — Board the late-afternoon Shinkansen back to Tokyo (Green Car reserved). Arrive in time for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner near your hotel or explore a local izakaya for a more casual end to a deeply meaningful day.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or a premium ekiben purchased at Tokyo Station for the Shinkansen journey.
meals.lunch: Kakifuku — A celebrated Hiroshima restaurant specializing in the region's famous oysters, served grilled, fried, or raw. Hiroshima is Japan's top oyster-producing region.
meals.dinner: Ukai Toriyama (うかい鳥山) — A spectacular restaurant in a traditional farmhouse setting in Hachioji (accessible from Tokyo), serving charcoal-grilled chicken kaiseki in a garden with koi ponds and traditional architecture. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day — depart Tokyo by 7:00–8:00 AM Shinkansen for maximum time in Hiroshima and Miyajima. The Peace Memorial Museum is emotionally intense; prepare children in advance with age-appropriate context. The floating torii gate is best viewed at high tide — check tide tables in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka Historic District — Explore Yanaka, one of Tokyo's last remaining shitamachi (old downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander the peaceful cemetery (Yanaka Reien) with its ancient cherry trees, browse independent craft shops and galleries along Yanaka Ginza shopping street, and experience a Tokyo that feels untouched by modernity — a perfect final cultural immersion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Akihabara & Imperial Palace East Gardens — Visit Akihabara for a fascinating glimpse into Japan's technology and pop culture universe (electronics, anime, gaming). Then visit the Imperial Palace East Gardens, the former grounds of Edo Castle, for a serene afternoon walk through manicured gardens and historic stone walls — a dignified and reflective final afternoon in Japan.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Preparations — Enjoy a spectacular farewell dinner at one of Tokyo's finest restaurants. Return to your hotel to pack and prepare for departure. Your luxury hotel concierge will arrange a private airport transfer for your outbound flight.

meals.breakfast: Final in-hotel luxury breakfast — savor a full Japanese breakfast (washoku) with grilled fish, miso soup, rice, pickles, and tamagoyaki, or a Western option as preferred.
meals.lunch: Yanaka Gyoza Fukuchan — A beloved local spot in Yanaka for handmade gyoza, or Kayaba Coffee — a historic 1938 café serving nostalgic Japanese kissaten-style coffee and egg sandwiches.
meals.dinner: Joël Robuchon Tokyo (Yebisu Garden Place) — The legendary French chef's Tokyo outpost in a stunning château setting, offering the ultimate multi-course L'Atelier experience. Alternatively, Saito — an ultra-exclusive, reservation-only sushi counter considered among the finest in the world, bookable only through top hotel concierges.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and arrange the airport transfer at least 3 hours before scheduled departure. Use the final morning to collect any remaining omiyage (souvenirs) — Yanaka Ginza is ideal for artisan gifts. Tax-free shopping is available at most department stores with your passport.
